acquisition_method: A data dependent mass spectrometric method was employed, where the 10 most intense ions, excluding unassigned charge states and singly charged ions, detected in the preceding full scan are isolated (3 Th isolation width) and fragmented using higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD)
alkylation_concentration: After reduction (5 mM DTT, 30 min) and alkylation (10 mM iodoacetamide, 20 min, in the dark), proteins were digested
alkylation_reagent: After reduction (5 mM DTT, 30 min) and alkylation (10 mM iodoacetamide, 20 min, in the dark), proteins were digested
cleavage_agent: proteins were digested for 3 h by Lys-C (Wako) at a protein:enzyme ratio of 100:1. Samples were diluted with 10 mM ammonium bicarbonate to 2 M urea prior to overnight trypsin digestion (Sequencing grade, Promega) at a protein:enzyme ratio of 100:1.
collision_energy: fragmented using higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD) (normalized collision energy 25)
fractionation_method: Peptides (180 μg) were separated by in-solution isoelectric focusing (OFFGEL fractionator, Agilent) into 12 fractions over a pH range of 3–10.
fragmentation_method: fragmented using higher energy collisional dissociation (HCD)

instrument.evidence: liquid chromatography (LC) using an EASY nLC-II coupled to a Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany)

labeling: quantitative high resolution nano-LC-MS/MS based on stable isotope labeling with amino acid in cell culture (SILAC)
mass_analyzer: inferred: Q Exactive mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific, Bremen, Germany)

ptm.evidence: N-terminal acetylation and methionine oxidation as variable modifications and cysteine carbamidomethylation as fixed modification
ptm.ontology_name: methionine oxidation with neutral loss of 80 Da

reduction_concentration: After reduction (5 mM DTT, 30 min) and alkylation
reduction_reagent: After reduction (5 mM DTT, 30 min) and alkylation
